To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the usage of ULM packages to model the relationships among design artifacts in different abstraction levels, allows the designer to provide complementary views in the same model.
we have designed a UML extension to model attributes as a first-class citizens and a framework for the modeling and design of data mappings in different levels of details.

(1) we have extended UML to support the design of data warehouses at different levels of granularity; (2) we have proposed a disciplined framework for modeling data warehouse design at different levels of detail; and (3) we have presented an application of this framework in the design of an ETL process for a data warehouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of DW back-stages, and the ETL processes that implement them.
the design of the back-stage of DWs, with the goal of facilitating the understanding and the maintenance of the ETL processes.

the development of an integrated framework for DW design that allows the modeling of the DW backstage in detail, while providing a comprehensive and coherent view of the design at different levels of granularity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of UML packages to represent different levels of granularity in the design of data mapping diagrams, is a promising and practical approach to the development of data warehouse design artifacts, which can be used as the basis for further refinements in the development of ETL processes.
the UML package concept can be exploited as a powerful means for providing complementary views of a scenario in different levels of abstraction and granularity.

we have developed a framework for the specification of the relationships between source and target attributes that allows for the modeling of different levels of granularity and the use of different views of these relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a framework for the modeling and design of ETL processes in DW scenarios, which is supported by the usage of the Unified Modeling Language (UML), and which is based on the key idea that the modeling of data mappings should be done at the attribute level, and that the relationships between sources, targets, and attributes are the key to the design of ETL scenarios.
it provides a framework for the specification of mappings at different levels of granularity, and the usage of Uml packages to model these mappings in different levels of abstraction.
our framework provides the necessary tools for the design of DW back-stage at different levels of granularity and for different levels of abstraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modeling of attribute-level transformations is a crucial step in the design of the back-stage of DW scenarios.

the design of DW back-stage can be accomplished with a rigorous and disciplined approach that allows for the modeling of different aspects of the scenario in different levels of abstraction and detail.
UML can serve as a very useful tool in DW design, as it provides a flexible framework for the representation of the design artifacts at different levels of granularity, and for their evolution.
